content.value_statement: Breaking Convex schema changes can fail deploys or damage production data. This skill guides safe rollouts, batched backfills, dry runs, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Convex schema changes require migrations.
Guides widen-migrate-narrow deployment plans for breaking changes.
Shows how to use @convex-dev/migrations for batched, resumable migrations.
Provides examples for adding fields, removing fields, changing types, and splitting tables.
Includes dry-run, status monitoring, cancellation, and verification guidance.
Highlights common pitfalls such as large collect calls and premature field deletion.
limitations: Does not connect to a Convex deployment or inspect live data by itself.
Requires the user to review generated migration logic before running it.
Examples must be adapted to each app schema, indexes, and production traffic.
Does not replace backups, dry runs, or staging validation for critical data.

use_cases.title: Add Required Fields Safely
use_cases.description: Plan a rollout that adds optional fields first, backfills existing documents, then makes fields required after verification.

use_cases.title: Prepare Zero Downtime Rollouts
use_cases.description: Design staged deploys where application code handles old and new data formats during migration windows.

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Data Models
use_cases.description: Map steps for field deletion, type changes, table splitting, orphan cleanup, and migration completion checks.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Migration Need
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before changing a schema.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Convex schema change and tell me whether it needs a data migration. Explain the deployment order and main risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Required Field Rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate plan for adding a field to existing documents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a widen-migrate-narrow plan for adding a required field to an existing Convex table. Include verification and rollback notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Batched Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use of the migrations component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a batched Convex migration with dry run, status monitoring, and safe batch sizing for this table.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Convex migration plan for production safety. Check schema widening, dual reads or writes, dry run coverage, and completion checks.

output_examples.input: A user table needs a new required role field for existing accounts.
output: Deploy a widened schema with role optional.
Backfill missing roles in batches with a dry run first.
Verify no accounts remain unmigrated before making role required.

output_examples.input: A team table is changing from a boolean plan flag to a plan enum.
output: Add the new plan field while keeping the old flag optional.
Write new documents in the new format during the transition.
Remove old readers and fields only after verification passes.

output_examples.input: A large table migration keeps timing out during local tests.
output: Use the migrations component instead of collecting the whole table.
Lower the batch size for heavy documents or high write traffic.
Monitor migration status and retry from the saved cursor after failures.

best_practices: Widen the schema before touching production data.
Run a dry run and inspect status before production execution.
Verify every document is migrated before narrowing the schema.
anti_patterns: Making a field required before existing documents are backfilled.
Using collect on large tables instead of a batched migration.
Deleting legacy fields before readers and writers stop using them.

faq.question: What is widen-migrate-narrow?
faq.answer: It is a staged workflow. First allow old and new data, then migrate records, then require the new shape.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides plans and examples. You choose when to run commands and should review them first.

faq.question: When should I use @convex-dev/migrations?
faq.answer: Use it for non-trivial backfills, large tables, resumable jobs, dry runs, and progress monitoring.

faq.question: Can it help with zero downtime?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains staged deploys, dual reads, dual writes, and verification before narrowing a schema.

faq.question: Does it support small table migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes when a single internal mutation can be acceptable for small tables.

faq.question: What should I do before production?
faq.answer: Back up important data, run a dry run, check migration status, and verify remaining unmigrated documents.
